title: Vault Guardian: choose the visual world
question: Player screen, Level IV mid-game, with the new prompt budget and New game button. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Arcane Vault Door
options.lineage: Dwarven vault doors and bank-safe combination dials, engraved in bronze
options.thesis: The game is a door with seven tumblers; every level you solve turns one into place.
options.viewport: Left half: the round door, seven concentric rings; the password slot sits in the hub. Right half: the guardian's dialogue as engraved speech, with the prompt budget in bronze pips.
options.risk: Tips into steampunk costume if the rings stop doing work; the circular door needs a stacked layout on phones.

raised.raise: One guardian owns the whole right half; no level list competes with the conversation.
Prompt budget is a row of identical pips, read as a ruler at a glance.
Ring state is carried by notch shape (aligned, turned, hollow), never by colour alone.
Ember orange is reserved for the one live tumbler and for a ward that fired.

options.label: The Dialogue Box
options.lineage: 16-bit JRPG text windows (Dragon Quest, Final Fantasy)
options.thesis: Talking an NPC into giving something up is the oldest JRPG move; the interface is that text window.
options.viewport: A world-map strip of seven towers on top, the guardian sprite in the middle, the dialogue window below, and a TALK / GUESS / NEW GAME command menu on the right.
options.risk: Familiar: every engineer at the stand knows it at once, and that is also why it reads as nostalgia rather than as its own thing.

options.label: The Title Sequence
options.lineage: Saul Bass title sequences, in cut paper
options.thesis: Each level is an act with its own flat colour field and a cut-paper guardian silhouette.
options.viewport: Giant tilted guardian name over a paper silhouette on the left; the conversation as stacked paper cards on the right; the field colour changes per level.
options.case: Carries the wizard fantasy through silhouettes and reads from across a conference hall; weaker on showing which ward fired.
options.risk: Seven different field colours have to stay legible; shapes need drawing, one per guardian.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.thesis: Every thread decision traceable to its punched row.
options.risk: Players do not identify with weaving.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the metaphor needs explaining at a booth.
options.kept: Every block is traceable to the ward that caused it.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Guard stages as a row of needles.
options.viewport: A bridge of meters over the chat.
options.case: Loses on audience fit: a studio, not a vault.
options.kept: Identical repeated units as a ruler (the prompt pips).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light chat app, the way Gandalf itself ships.
canonCard.viewport: Level list left, chat right, meter under the title, password field under the composer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design; drops the fantasy to decoration.
